name: Image-Charts
description: SaaS API that renders charts (static or animated) as images for emails, PDFs, reports, and chatbots — Zapier/Make friendly. Founded 2017, France. Business $89/mo yearly / Enterprise $224/mo yearly (company-stated).

mentions.evidence: ~$6.3k MRR, 50 active subscriptions, ~$2.4k L30, ~$541k all-time, founded Jan 2017. Last sync Sep 29, 2026.
mentions.indieAngle: Longevity proof — a narrow API can compound for a decade without chasing AI hype.

mentions.evidence: ~$6,281 MRR, 50 active subscriptions, ~$2,343 L30, ~$541,380 all-time. Revenue synced Oct 12, 2026 ~04:25 Warsaw.
mentions.indieAngle: Sell a single developer utility as an image CDN for charts — high all-time, low feature churn, Zapier distribution.

whyItPrints: Embedding interactive charts in email clients is a nightmare; a URL that returns a PNG/GIF is the boring fix. Nine-year-old API with half a million all-time is quiet glue revenue.
whyThisMatters:
Email clients can't run a live chart. Image-Charts turns the chart into a picture and gives you a URL. That picture can sit in an email, a PDF, a report, or a chat. It's the job Google Image Charts used to do. The company has been bootstrapped since 2017.

If you don't code, Zapier and Make can build the image from a form, a Google Sheet, Drive, Dropbox, or Pipedrive. If you do code, there's an API. Each chart has its own URL. It's built to answer in under a second. You set it up once and leave it.

Lines, bars, pies, donuts, sparklines, and QR codes are included. One QR code is for joining a Wi-Fi network. A free editor adds a small watermark. Paid plans remove it, add your own subdomain, and turn on Zapier and Make. A higher plan draws charts with more than one axis. If the data has to stay on your network, there's an on-premise machine. Microsoft, Spotify, and Dropbox use it.

You've already got the numbers. This puts them where a live chart won't load.

You pass a URL and get back a chart image for the report.
